title: Essential Singularity of the Correlation Length in the Planar XY Model
note: Automated manuscript extraction. Mathematical correctness and proof completeness have not been independently checked.
abstract: We prove the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless essential singularity for the correlation length of the nearest-neighbor cosine XY model on the square lattice. Let $m(b)$ be the mass obtained by taking first the free-box thermodynamic limit and then the separation limit along a coordinate axis. As the inverse temperature b approaches bc from the massive side, $\displaystyle \sqrt{b_c-b}\log\frac{1}{m(b)} \longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{XY}},$ where $A_{\mathrm{XY}}$ is a finite, strictly positive model-specific constant.
sourceAbstract: We prove the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless essential singularity for the correlation length of the nearest-neighbor cosine XY model on the square lattice. Let \(m(b)\) be the mass obtained by taking first the free-box thermodynamic limit and then the separation limit along a coordinate axis. As the inverse temperature \(b\) approaches \(b_c\) from the massive side, \[ \sqrt{b_c-b}\log\frac{1}{m(b)} \longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{XY}}, \] where \(A_{\mathrm{XY}}\) is a finite, strictly positive model-specific constant.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text: For the model \eqref{eq:spin-law}, there is a constant $A_{\mathrm{XY}}\in(0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \lim_{b\uparrow b_c}\sqrt{b_c-b}\,\log\xi(b)=A_{\mathrm{XY}}. \end{equation}

statements.name: Analytic initialization
statements.label: prop:entry
statements.text: For every sufficiently small $\rho>0$, the fixed choices above can be made so that there exist $c_{R_0}>0$ and $s_0<\infty$ with the following property. For every admissible $s\ge s_0$, the ordinary plane and compatible-torus entry activities $K_s(b)$ are Banach analytic on \begin{equation} |b-\bc|<c_{R_0}s^{-2}, \end{equation} and take values in $\mathscr A^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{L^{j_0},s}$ or its compatible-torus counterpart, with norm at most $\rho$. They are real on real fields when $b$ is real. Their support, symmetry, and local copying identities agree with those at criticality throughout the complex parameter disk. For real parameters in this disk the cutoff partition representation is exact. On a smaller concentric disk, for each fixed $r\ge1$, \begin{equation} \|\partial_b^rK_s(b)\|_{L^{j_0},s} \le C_{R_0,r}s^{2r}. \end{equation}

statements.name: Activity map
statements.label: prop:map
statements.text: For all sufficiently large absolute indices $j$, the map on $(t,z,\mathcal R)\in\mathbb C^2\times \mathscr A^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{L^j,s}$, with the occupied-support and designated-localization conventions of \cite[Proposition 4.1]{F}, preserves the bulk symmetry class and is analytic on a fixed ball $|t|+|z|+\|\mathcal R\|_{L^j,s}<\rho_{\mathrm{map}}$. Its linear part is \begin{equation} (t,z,\mathcal R)\longmapsto (t+P_j^t\mathcal R,\lambda_jz+P_j^z\mathcal R, \mathsf C_j\mathcal R), \quad \|\mathsf C_j\|\le\theta_0<1, \quad \lambda_j=1+O(e^{-cj}), \end{equation} with uniformly bounded rows $P_j^t,P_j^z$. The nonlinear part and its Taylor derivatives have quadratic bounds with uniform constants. There are analytic normal coordinates $(u,Z,Q)$, uniform in the entry side, such that the pure Gaussian curve is $(u,0,0)$ and the map fixes $u$ on that curve. With $b_*=2\log L$ and a constant $H>0$, define \begin{equation} x=b_*u,\qquad y=\sqrt{b_*H}\,Z,\qquad W=(x,y). \end{equation} The coordinate changes obey \begin{equation} t=u+O(u^2+\|Q\|),\qquad z=(1+O(e^{-cj}))Z+O(u^2+\|Q\|),\qquad \mathcal R=O(u^2)+Q, \end{equation} with the differentiated analytic bounds of these orders. In a fixed small tube, \begin{equation} \begin{split} W_+&=W+(-y^2,-xy)+\mathcal E_j(W,Q),\\ |\mathcal E_j(W,Q)| &\le C\{j^{-2}|W|^2+|W|^3+(|W|+\|Q\|)\|Q\|\},\\ \|Q_+\|&\le\theta\|Q\|+C|W|^2,\qquad \theta<1. \end{split} \end{equation} The error is an analytic function with the corresponding Taylor bounds on all fixed derivatives. On a separately initialized compatible torus with a fixed range buffer, the two singleton coefficients copy the plane coefficients through its stop. The torus remainder has its own contraction and analytic quadratic bound. Its derivative at zero has no singleton forcing. All constants are uniform in the stop, the entry side, and their associated norms.

statements.label: prop:readouts
statements.text:
On a fixed small complex ball of terminal activities, the cutoff variance correction and the cutoff phase expectation extend to analytic functions of the activity coordinates. If $

The multipliers are positive, bounded above and below, and  egin{equation} v^0_{n,s}=a\mathfrak g+O(s/n+n^{-2}),\qquad \kappa_{n,s}=a\mathfrak g+O(s/n+n^{-2}). \end{equation} At a common absolute stop, the multipliers $p_{j,s}$ for different entries agree except for their mean-observation-noise factor; their relative difference is $O((s_1/n)^2+(s_2/n)^2)$.

statements.name: Critical histories
statements.label: prop:critical
statements.text: The fixed parameters and entry threshold can be chosen so that there is a family $\mathcal H^{(k)}$ at $b=\bc$, with admissible $s_k\asymp2^k$ and entry indices $j_0(k)=O(k)$, having the following properties. For every fixed $0<c<c'<3$, uniformly on $c2^k\le j\le c'2^k$, \begin{equation} W_j^{(k)}=\frac{(1,1)}j+O\!\left(\frac{\log(2+j)}{j^2}\right), \qquad \|Q_j^{(k)}\|+\|\mathcal R_j^{(k)}\|=O(j^{-2}). \end{equation} The separately initialized torus remainders also satisfy $O(j^{-2})$ on these stage ranges behind every valid later stop in the same history up to $4\cdot2^k$. More generally, for any prescribed sufficiently small tube and any integer bound $J_{\max}(s)=o(s^2)$, the critical plane history at an admissible side $s$ stays in that tube through $J_{\max}(s)$, for all large $s$. Every stage of its separately initialized tori with valid stops below $J_{\max}(s)$ stays in the corresponding small ball. The choices of geometric parameters are independent of $s$ and $J_{\max}$.

statements.name: Nonzero temperature response
statements.label: prop:response
statements.text: For the fixed choices above there is a number \(\mathcal P\in(0,\infty)\) such that, with \[ V_j^{(k)}= \left.\frac{\partial W_j^{(k)}(b)}{\partial b}\right|_{b=\bc}, \qquad q_u=(1,-\tfrac12), \] we have \begin{equation} \sup_{\frac12 2^k\le j\le\frac52 2^k} \left|\frac{V_j^{(k)}}j-\mathcal Pq_u\right| \longrightarrow0. \end{equation} The plane transverse remainder and every separately initialized torus remainder, at an index in this range behind a valid stop in the critical history, have temperature derivative bounded by \(C|V_j^{(k)}|/j+e^{-cj}\).

statements.name: Passage time and the variance diagnostic
statements.label: prop:passage
statements.text: Put \[ k_0=\sqrt{3\mathcal P},\qquad T=\frac\pi{k_0}. \] For \(b=\bc-\eps\), use an admissible observation side \(s\asymp\eps^{-1/3}\). On every compact subinterval of \((0,T)\), the scalar trajectory satisfies, uniformly for \(w=\delta j\) in that subinterval, \begin{equation} \frac{x_j(b)}\delta\longrightarrow k_0\cot(k_0w), \qquad \frac{y_j(b)}\delta\longrightarrow k_0\csc(k_0w), \qquad \|Q_j(b)\|=O(\delta^2). \end{equation} In particular, for every sequence \(\eps\downarrow0\) and \(\delta j\to w\in(0,T)\), \begin{equation} \Var_{b,n_j}^{\mathrm{tor}}H_{n_j} \longrightarrow a\mathfrak g. \end{equation} For every sufficiently small fixed \(d>0\), there are exit indices \(j_e=j_e(\eps,d)\) such that \begin{equation} \delta j_e\longrightarrow T,\qquad x_{j_e}=-d+O(d^2),\qquad y_{j_e}=O(d),\qquad \|Q_{j_e}\|+\|\mathcal R_{j_e|j_e}^{\mathrm{tor}}\|=O(d^2). \end{equation} All states through the exit lie in the small-activity map domain. For some \(c_d>0\), \begin{equation} \limsup_{\eps\downarrow0} \Var_{b,n_{j_e}}^{\mathrm{tor}}H_{n_{j_e}} \le a\mathfrak g-c_d. \end{equation} The torus law in these assertions is the original periodic Bessel height law in the zero-winding sector, with its common height translation factored out.

statements.name: Extraction on logarithmic scales
statements.label: prop:profile
statements.text: Every sequence $b_k\to\bc$ from below has a subsequence and a nonincreasing function $\mathcal A:(0,\infty)\to[0,a]$, where $a=8\pi$, with the following property. At each continuity point $w>0$ of $\mathcal A$, every integer sequence $m_k$ satisfying $\delta_k\log_L m_k\to w$ obeys \begin{equation} a_{m_k}(b_k)\longrightarrow\mathcal A(w). \end{equation} One may choose $\mathcal A$ to be right continuous.

statements.name: Gaussian laws at continuity scales
statements.label: prop:gaussian-profile
statements.text: Let $w$ be a continuity point of the extracted profile, let $\delta_k\log_Ln_k\to w$, and put $a_*=\mathcal A(w)$. The free rectangular limits are those in Lemma \ref{lem:profile-free}; if $a_*>0$, their fractional means have the conclusion of Lemma \ref{lem:profile-phase}, and their fixed primary pinned geometries have the Gaussian Laplace and moment limits of Lemma \ref{lem:profile-pins}. In particular, on a square interior surrounded by a fixed positive-width zero rim, the covariance of bounded piecewise continuous density smears converges to $a_*(-\Delta_D)^{-1}$, with Dirichlet boundary on that square. On the zero-winding height torus of side $n_k$, every smooth periodic shift $g$ satisfies \begin{equation} \Var(h,A_{\mathrm{tor}}g_k)\longrightarrow a_*\int_{\mathbb T^2}|\nabla g|^2. \end{equation} Thus the area-weighted first cosine observation in \eqref{eq:physical-cosine} has limiting variance $a_*\mathfrak g$, where $\mathfrak g=1/(8\pi^2)$.

statements.name: Uniform affine transforms on a zero interval
statements.label: cor:profile-zero-uniform
statements.text: Suppose $I=[u,v]\subset(0,\infty)$ consists of continuity points of $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A=0$ on $I$. Fix a compact set $K\subset\R^2$ and $\lambda\in\R$. For a free square of side $m$ write $X_{m,p}=(h,A_{B_m}(p\cdot x/m))$. Then \begin{equation} \sup_{\substack{m\in\N:\ \delta_k\log_Lm\in I\\p\in K}} \left|\E_{B_m,b_k}^{\mathrm{free}}e^{\lambda X_{m,p}}-1\right| \longrightarrow0. \end{equation} The assertion is unchanged by translating the squares or multiplying their sides by factors in a fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$, provided their resulting logarithmic scales stay in a fixed zero-profile neighborhood of $I$.

statements.name: The profile has one jump, at the passage time
statements.label: prop:profile-step
statements.text: The profile extracted in Proposition \ref{prop:profile} satisfies \begin{equation} \mathcal A(w)=a\quad(0<w<T),\qquad \mathcal A(w)=0\quad(w>T), \qquad T=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3\mathcal P}}. \end{equation} In particular all points of these two open intervals are continuity points. No assertion about its value at the single point $T$ is needed.

statements.label: prop:mass-polynomial
statements.text: Fix \(w'>T\), positive integers \(r_k\) satisfying \(\delta_k\log_Lr_k\to w'\), and constants \(0<c_0<C_0<\infty\). For every \(K>0\), all sufficiently large \(k\) satisfy \begin{equation} \sup_{c_0r_k\le\|x\|_\infty\le C_0r_k}C_{b_k}(x) \le r_k^{-K}. \end{equation}
